selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: It explains that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is without equal in the religion he brought, in worship, in prayer, and in knowing Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the law he brought?
questions.answer: It says that no other law is like it in fairness, careful guidance, and lasting influence over many people for a very long time.

questions.question: Why is it important that he was unlettered?
questions.answer: It makes his achievement even more amazing, because he brought great guidance without learning it from books or teachers in the usual way.

questions.question: How did Islam help people, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It guided their minds, gave safety and direction, cleaned and brightened their hearts, trained their souls, and helped their spirits grow.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Prophet’s worship?
questions.answer: It says he was the best example in doing acts of worship, being careful of Allah, and carrying out worship fully even during hard times.

questions.question: How is his worship shown to be special?
questions.answer: He practiced every part of worship in the best way and did not copy another person.

questions.question: What does the passage say about his prayers and du'as?
questions.answer: It says his prayers show a very deep knowledge of Allah that later saints and people of spiritual understanding could not reach together.

questions.question: What does this teach us about the Jawshan al-Kabir?
questions.answer: It teaches that this du'a is very special and has no equal in the way it speaks about Allah.

questions.question: If later holy people could not match his knowledge of Allah in prayer, what can we infer about him?
questions.answer: We can infer that he had a very high and unique closeness in knowing and describing his Lord.

questions.question: Which parts of life does the passage use to show his greatness?
questions.answer: It uses religious law, Islam as a way of life, worship, piety, and supplication.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kinds of things did the Prophet bring to people?
questions.answer: He brought a sacred law, Islam, worship, a mission, a call to truth, and faith.

questions.question: How does the passage describe these things compared with anything else?
questions.answer: It says nothing equal to them exists, and nothing more complete can exist.

questions.question: What proof from history is given for the strength of his law?
questions.answer: It ruled a large part of humanity with justice and care for fourteen centuries.

questions.question: What effect did Islam have on people in each century?
questions.answer: It taught their minds, protected and guided them, purified their hearts, trained their inner selves, and helped them progress.

questions.question: What can we learn from the passage about true religion?
questions.answer: True religion helps the whole person, not only actions but also the mind, heart, soul, and spirit.

questions.question: How did the Prophet act in worship while living an active and difficult life?
questions.answer: He still gave full attention to worship and carried out its deepest meanings.

questions.question: What is meant by saying he joined the beginning and end of worship perfectly?
questions.answer: It means he completed worship in the best way from start to finish, with full servanthood to Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that he did not imitate anyone?
questions.answer: To show that his worship was original, complete, and unmatched.

questions.question: What special example of his prayer is named in the passage?
questions.answer: The Jawshan al-Kabir is named.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage lead the reader to about the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.answer: It leads the reader to see that he is unmatched in guiding people and in serving Allah.

questions.question: Who is the passage mainly talking about?
questions.answer: It is mainly talking about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

questions.question: In what area does the passage first say he has no equal?
questions.answer: It first says he has no equal in the law and religion he brought.

questions.question: How long does the passage say his law has guided people?
questions.answer: It says for fourteen centuries.

questions.question: About how many people in each century are said to have been guided by Islam?
questions.answer: About three hundred million people.
